long_biography.plain_text:
Francisco Hernando grew up in extreme poverty in Madrid's Tetuán district and began earning money while still a child. He carried water to building workers, cleaned sewers beside his father and saved for tools to establish an independent drainage operation. Haulage work at Mercamadrid led him into trucks and concrete mixers, then into apartment construction. He eventually assembled the ONDE 2000 property group and became widely known by the nickname Paco el Pocero.

His boldest undertaking was El Quiñón at Seseña, a planned residential district of more than 13,000 homes south of Madrid. Thousands of apartments and extensive infrastructure rose before the Spanish property crash disrupted sales, financing and completion. The development became a national symbol of both the ambition and excess of the boom. Hernando later pursued proposed projects in Equatorial Guinea and other overseas markets, but none displaced Spanish residential development as his defining business. He died in Madrid in 2020.
